Instructions for New Moderators AKA How to be a Goat Herder

Moderators are like Goat Herders. Like in many traditional trades, they often wore distinctive hats to mark their trade.

The following is a collection of ideas, suggestions, and rules so that you can wear your VOAT Goat Herder Hat with pride

We will try to add to this post, without being encyclopedic

Important Stuff

  • Atko's Statement on Questionable Content

Principals for Moderators

TL;DR rule:

  • Good moderation creates a good community that is growing well.
  • Bad Moderation disrupts the community and users and make enemies out of everyone.

Please Note

  • This Post has to do with basic information for dealing with people
  • This Post does not cover general Voat TOS and other Voat policies
  • This Post will not contain information for configuring your subverse
  • This post will not contain information for editing your CSS for your subverse

Goat Orientation

  • Parts breakdown
  • Basics of Goat Safety

Basic Rules of Thumb for All Users

  • This is a new place
  • Everyone put down the weapons and take a deep breath
  • Leave the old BS and bad attitudes and bad habits at the old place
  • Wheaton's Rule applies: Don't Be a Dick
  • Remember that both civility and nastiness are contagious
  • You should be familiar with and use the data in the post Information for New Users
  • If you see a person making a mistake in VOAT etiquette, gently correct and educate them, and maybe also point them to the post Information for New Users

On freedom in general

  • Freedom is power
  • Freedom is certainly the ability to exercise power, the ability to do things
  • It is well known in popular culture that with great power comes great responsibility
  • Thus with great freedom comes great responsibility
  • Because of the great freedom you have as a moderator of the community you are involved with, you then have the responsibility to help create, maintain, and safeguard that community.
  • If you do not act to help create, maintain, and safeguard that community, it can come back to bite you and make your life miserable.
  • If you are miserable as a moderator, you will eventually end up sabotaging the freedom you are trying to protect.
  • To protect freedom, you have to protect the free community.
  • To protect your happiness as a moderator, you have to protect the free community.

More Notes on Freedom

  • Especially as a moderator at VOAT you are protecting the free community.
  • A free community can get very wild and very messy.
  • To protect the free community, sometimes you have to act against people endangering the community.
  • To protect the free community, most of the time you are gently encouraging Freespech and civility
  • Free speech is not the enemy of civility. Civility is not the enemy of Free speech.
  • Free speech is not the enemy of coarse language. Coarse language is not the enemy of Free speech.
  • Rudeness is often used to shock. Coarse and offensive language can often enhance actual discussion.
  • Rude, coarse, and insuting language can also be used to corrupt a discussion, forcing it gradually into a circle jerk.
  • If something is rude and off topic, then handle it on the basis of "it's off topic", not because it rude.
  • Excessive civility is sometimes used to avoid "hard to discuss" and "uncomfortable" topics. (I.E. - We do not talk about stuff like that here)
  • Remember that both civility and nastiness are contagious.

In the context of free speech, certain kinds of free speech disrupt the community, and destroy the "commons" that is the community forum. Some folks have cited the speech of people like comedian Joan Rivers, Lenny Bruce, and Artist Frank Zappa as justifications for disruptive, harmful, and disrupting behavior. Of course, if these people were as bright and capable as Joan Rivers, Lenny Bruce, or Frank Zappa, there would not be a problem with their speech. These people were geniuses. This is a high standard, because not everyone is a genius.

Brilliance in the form of revered artists is not an excuse for untalented unskilled unprincipled insult.

There is a concept/text from the early days of the internet know as the Tragedy of the Commons The tragedy of the commons is a term, originally used by Garrett Hardin, to describe a situation where individuals acting independently and rationally according to self-interest behave contrary to the best interests of the whole group by depleting some common resource. Thus you get problems like overfishing, overpopulation, pollution, etc.

In absence of enlightened self-interest, some form of authority, rules, etc are needed to solve the collective action problem.

The general principles are therefore

  • encourage and grow "enlightened self interest"
  • encourage and grow excellence in discussion
  • use rules and regulations lightly, only using a heavy hand when forced.
  • do not be afraid to act when you have exceptionally abusive users.
  • check with other more experienced mods if you have questions.

Basic Rules of Thumb for Dealing with Users

  • Moderators also have to abide with the general rules for Users.
  • Wheaton's Rule applies: Don't Be a Dick
  • Remember that both civility and nastiness are contagious
  • People tend to have a strong sense of fairness and justice. They get angry when you violate this. In some cases this can even feel like a form of rape. Therefore
  • Base decisions on good fundamental written principals
  • Enforce the subverse rules as they are written
  • Do not enforce rules that are not written or are not published.
  • Do not make up rules "because it seems like a good idea"
  • Do not surprise the users with new rules unannounced.
  • Do not delete comments or posts because they go against unwritten/unpublished rules
  • Do not hound the users with arbitrary rules.
  • Do not violate VOAT rules for your own personal pleasure or purposes.
  • Do not DOX or otherwise harrass users.

Otherwise you will be the thankless target of hate and scorn.

Dealing with disruptive or confrontational users

There are different kinds of disruptive users

  • As noted by Alfred

Alfred Pennyworth: Well, because he thought it was good sport. Because some men aren't looking for anything logical, like money. They can't be bought, bullied, reasoned, or negotiated with. Some men just want to watch the world burn. * Some people get insulted by the concept of any rules whatsoever. * Angry users with a pet cause or a pet peeve from outside of Voat (Politics, Social Justice, etc) * Users angry due to some perceived insult or injustice on VOAT * Users angry due to poor moderation.

It is important to correctly identify what kind of person you are dealing with, and then choose the correct method for dealing with them.

It is important to have rules written in advance.

It is important not just to have rules, but to understand why the rules are there, so that you can make adjustments if your rules have mistakes, etc.

Your choices are

Rewarding excellent work

  • with promotion
  • with a separate post calling out the good work and praising it. (note /v/BestOf, etc)

Encouraging by

  • positive comments and upvoating.
  • using them as a good example in other discussions.
  • setting a good example

Discourage the bad behavior by

  • warning
  • education
  • extended education
  • penalty

Stopping the bad behavior by

  • forced correction, deletions, etc.
  • announcement of new rules, other announcements, etc.
  • temp ban
  • report to other mods, etc
  • temporary ban that is publically announced with justifications and links to evidence, etc.
  • permanent ban that is publically announced with justifications and links to evidence, etc.

There is some argument on if bans should be public or secret. Secret/shadow bans need to be discussed.

Deleting/removing a post or comment, on the basis of "this is not what I want, but it's not in the rules" is a technique guaranteed to offend and makes for bad feelings all around.

  • It is generally better to use both rewards and punishments. Do not just beat your subverse into submission.

Things to think about

  • The Secret Garden - Attaining Your CCP Thresholds
  • Have Your Say on VOAT -- Why can't I be a dick?
  • Avoid being a Dick - Notes on How People Have Arguments
  • Links related to G.I.F.T. (Greater Internet Fuckwad Theory)

Moderator Resources Links to Subverses

  • /v/ModHelp
  • /v/NeedAMod
  • /v/Mods (Mod talk)
  • /v/ModAbuse
  • /v/Modtraining
  • /v/moderators
  • /v/Mod
  • /v/ModLounge
  • /v/ModDiscussion
  • /v/FindAMod
  • /v/badmods

There are also a number of subverses for mods of individual subverses such as /v/newsmods, /v/AskVoatMods, etc

Offsite Links that might be helpful:

  • Anger Management - the Art of Forum Moderation
  • The Art of Hosting Good Conversations Online By Howard Rheingold
  • Online book: Howard Rheingold's The Virtual Community
  • The Confessions of a Former Troll
